messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO alert - dedicated pool saturation detected in eu-west-1 (pool-id: pool-az3-eu). p99 gen latency 4.8s (SLO 3s), p95 2.2s. Streaming stalls observed for chat streams. Queue depth spiked from ~12 -> ~480 in the last 3m. Trigger: autoscaler warmup timeouts + cold-slot backlog. Thread TS 6578901234

alice: taking pager. landing in #incidents warroom. oncall handoff: running initial checks. who's closest to autoscaler logs?

jordan: I can grab logs, looking at autoscaler now. seeing repeated "warmup_timeout" in autoscaler-controller for pool-az3-eu: "warmup_timeout=90s slots_not_ready=12/20". Also kube nodes show some GPU drivers restarted ~2m ago.

lin: I see increased scheduling latency on the internal scheduler, pods stuck in ContainerCreating for ~40-70s. nv_peer_mem errors in node logs for two machines (az3-eu-07, az3-eu-08).

ash: packet: rolling hardware flake? telemetry shows elevated kernel oops 10:14:22-10:16:00 UTC. Could be transient causing slow slot readiness.

alice: ok immediate plan (runbook-lite): 1) enable emergency fallback routing for latency-sensitive customers 2) scale pool manually to drain queue 3) cordon/replace unhealthy nodes 4) notify CS and customers if impact confirmed.

maya: I have DM from two paying customers (Acme & BrightShop) reporting streaming stalls and partial responses. both on dedicated pools in eu-west. Acme on gen endpoint, BrightShop on chat. Severity: customer-visible but partial degradation. I'll prepare an outbound message draft.

jordan: running commands now to inspect queue and autoscaler state:
```bash
# view pool state
rictl pools describe pool-az3-eu --output json | jq '.slots, .queue_depth'
# tail autoscaler logs
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/autoscaler-controller -l pool=pool-az3-eu --tail=200
```

jordan: logged: queue_depth=472, active_slots=8/20, pending_warmups=12, scale_attempts=3, last_scale_fail_reason="warmup_timeout"

alice: enable fallback for customers marked latency-critical: toggling route -> hosted-small fallback. Maya, can you confirm which customers need fallback?

maya: Acme = yes (latency-critical), BrightShop = maybe (ok with fallback for writes but needs chat continuity). Sending opt-in list now.

alice: executing manual scale up to buy time: `rictl pool scale --pool=pool-az3-eu --target-slots=28 --reason "incident: manual scale to drain backlog"`

jordan: autoscaler metrics show repeated warmup timeouts; manual scale attempt returns "provisioned 20 new slots, 6 failed to initialize (warmup_timeout)". New slots not immediately usable.

lin: working on node replacement. starting cordon + drain for az3-eu-07 and az3-eu-08. will reprovision with latest GPU driver and kernel patch.

ash: patching nodes now. noderepair job kicked off. estimate ~8-12m to bring substituted nodes online.

alice: quick mitigation: enable KV prefix cache bypass for streaming to reduce warmup pressure (best-effort). Jordan, could you flip cache bypass for affected model?

jordan: done: toggled `kv_cache.strategy=bypass` for model redwood-open-7b-quant in pool-az3-eu. Expecting reduced per-request initialization. Observed small drop in slot memory usage.

alice: also enabling emergency routing to hosted fallback for Acme and BrightShop. `rictl route set-fallback --customer=Acme --to=hosted-small --force`

maya: Acme confirmed switched to fallback, reports latency back to normal. BrightShop on fallback but seeing truncated streams occasionally — investigating with BrightShop SRE.

oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident acknowledged by oncall alice. Pager escalations paused while mitigation in progress.

jordan: monitoring p95/p99 now: p95 dropped from 2.2s -> 1.1s for routed customers. p99 across pool still ~3.9s due to remaining queue for non-fallback customers.

alice: if manual drains don't finish, next step is to enable aggressive de-prioritization of burst customers (hotshot throttling) and increase warmup timeout as temporary measure.

lin: replaced nodes are coming up, drivers reinstalled, pods starting and passing readiness. New slots reported ready=10 in last 5m.

jordan: good signal: queue depth down to 160, active_slots=26/28, pending_warmups=2. p99 trending down.

maya: customer impact summary for support: Acme - affected for ~12m, fallback applied, no data loss, refused requests retried. BrightShop - partial stalls for ~18m, fallback in progress, CS will follow up with postmortem. Draft outbound updated.

alice: declaring page handoff: monitoring mode. If p99 < 3s and queue < 50 for 10m, mark incident mitigated. Please add all post-incident follow-ups to the incident ticket.

ash: adding follow-ups: replace affected hardware fleet images, extend warmup timeout to 120s for pool-az3-eu as temporary config, add telemetry alerts for nv_peer_mem errors.

jordan: root-cause hypothesis: concurrent kernel/driver flake on two nodes caused warmup failures, autoscaler retried but hit warmup_timeout thresholds leading to slow manual provisioning and queue amplification under burst. Needs longer-term remediation in autoscaler + node health detection.

alice: agreed. Action items assigned: jordan -> write RCA draft, lin -> node image + validation, ash -> autoscaler warmup tuning + alerting, maya -> customer comms + support ticket updates. I'll keep incident open until we verify steady-state.

jordan: p99 now 2.0s, queue 38, sustaining. continuing to monitor.

alice: closing pager if nothing regresses in 15m. great work team. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: :lock: Incident escalations resumed to normal. Incident transitioned to post-mitigation monitoring.
